Identity.History:
Epaminondas was the foremost Theban statesman and general of the 4th century BC and one of the most innovative commanders of classical Greece. Rising to prominence after Thebes threw off Spartan domination, he helped transform the Boeotian army and, at the Battle of Leuctra in 371 BC, used an unusually deep left wing and an oblique deployment to crush the previously dominant Spartan army. The victory broke Sparta’s military prestige and opened the way for Theban intervention throughout Greece.
In the following years, Epaminondas repeatedly campaigned in the Peloponnese, helped liberate Messenia from Spartan control, and supported the foundation of Megalopolis as a counterweight to Sparta. He remained the driving force behind Theban power until 362 BC, when he won another major battle at Mantinea but was mortally wounded during the fighting. His death effectively ended the period of Theban supremacy, but his tactical innovations and strategic achievements had a lasting influence on Greek warfare.
